item.research_question: Can an entropy-forming-ability (EFA) descriptor based on first-principles energy distribution spectra predict the synthesizability of disordered five-metal refractory carbides as homogeneous high-entropy single phases?
item.material_system: Five-metal refractory carbides (MoNbTaVWC5, HfNbTaTiZrC5, HfNbTaTiVC5, HfNbTaTiWC5, NbTaTiVWC5, HfTaTiWZrC5, HfMoTaWZrC5, HfMoTiWZrC5, HfMoVWZrC5) derived from eight metals (Hf, Nb, Mo, Ta, Ti, V, W, Zr) and carbon
item.processing_route: Solid-state synthesis via ball milling (2 h total, 30-min intervals with 10-min rests) followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 2200 °C, 100 °C/min heating rate, 30 MPa uniaxial pressure, 5-min dwell in vacuum/argon atmosphere
item.test_conditions: X-ray diffraction (XRD) for phase identification; Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) for chemical homogeneity; Nanoindentation at 27 °C ± 0.5 °C with 50 mN load for Vickers hardness (HV) and elastic modulus (E); Williamson–Hall analysis for lattice strain
key_findings: The EFA descriptor correctly predicted that MoNbTaVWC5 (EFA = 125 (eV/atom)−1), HfNbTaTiZrC5 (EFA = 100 (eV/atom)−1), and HfNbTaTiVC5 (EFA = 100 (eV/atom)−1) would form homogeneous single phases, while HfMoVWZrC5 (EFA = 37 (eV/atom)−1) would not.

Six of the nine synthesized compositions (MoNbTaVWC5, HfNbTaTiZrC5, HfNbTaTiVC5, HfNbTaTiWC5, NbTaTiVWC5, HfTaTiWZrC5) exhibited single rock-salt fcc phases, whereas the three lowest-EFA compositions showed multiple secondary phases.
Vickers hardness of HfNbTaTiZrC5 reached 32 GPa, which is 50% higher than the rule of mixtures (ROM) prediction, and HfTaTiWZrC5 reached 33 GPa.
The Pearson correlation between the inverse EFA (EFA−1) and lattice distortion (ε) was 0.97, and the Spearman rank correlation was 0.98, validating EFA as a synthesizability descriptor.
Lattice distortion (ε) ranged from 0.063% for MoNbTaVWC5 (most homogeneous) to 0.325% for HfMoVWZrC5 (least homogeneous).

The highest-EFA composition MoNbTaVWC5 formed a homogeneous phase despite using precursors Mo2C and W2C with different structures (orthorhombic and hexagonal) and stoichiometries compared to the rock-salt product.

Vibrational contributions to formation free energy at 2000 K ranged from ~0 meV/atom to −31 meV/atom, which are significantly smaller than the configurational entropy contributions required to overcome formation enthalpy barriers (50–150 meV/atom).
A threshold of EFA ~50 (eV/atom)−1 was identified as the point above which homogeneous disordered single phases are likely to form.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that a narrow energy distribution spectrum (low standard deviation σ) implies a low energy cost to access metastable configurations, promoting configurational randomness (entropy) at finite temperatures. This entropy stabilization allows the disordered rock-salt phase to remain locked in upon cooling, even when competing ordered phases exist. Enhanced hardness is attributed to mass disorder causing impedance mismatch that scatters dislocations, increasing resistance to plastic deformation.
item.limitations: The study notes that the Williamson–Hall formalism does not provide particularly accurate absolute values of lattice strain (ε), though it is effective for relative comparisons. Additionally, the vibrational contribution to entropy is an order of magnitude smaller than configurational entropy, and the study did not investigate the specific effect of carbon stoichiometry on melting points.
item.future_work: The authors state that an investigation of the effect of carbon stoichiometry is clearly warranted to understand how vacancies might further improve high-temperature performance, although it is outside the scope of this study.
quotes: The descriptor correctly predicts the ease with which compositions can be experimentally synthesized as rock-salt high-entropy homogeneous phases, validating the ansatz, and in some cases, going beyond intuition.
Several of these materials exhibit hardness up to 50% higher than rule of mixtures estimations.
The Pearson (linear) correlation of EFA−1 with ε is 0.97, whereas the Spearman (rank order) correlation is 0.98.

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can an entropy-forming-ability (EFA) descriptor based on first-principles energy distribution spectra predict the synthesizability of disordered five-metal refractory carbides as homogeneous high-entropy single phases?. System: Five-metal refractory carbides (MoNbTaVWC5, HfNbTaTiZrC5, HfNbTaTiVC5, HfNbTaTiWC5, NbTaTiVWC5, HfTaTiWZrC5, HfMoTaWZrC5, HfMoTiWZrC5, HfMoVWZrC5) derived from eight metals (Hf, Nb, Mo, Ta, Ti, V, W, Zr) and carbon. Processing: Solid-state synthesis via ball milling (2 h total, 30-min intervals with 10-min rests) followed by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 2200 °C, 100 °C/min heating rate, 30 MPa uniaxial pressure, 5-min dwell in vacuum/argon atmosphere. Test conditions: X-ray diffraction (XRD) for phase identification; Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) for chemical homogeneity; Nanoindentation at 27 °C ± 0.5 °C with 50 mN load for Vickers hardness (HV) and elastic modulus (E); Williamson–Hall analysis for lattice strain. Findings: The EFA descriptor correctly predicted that MoNbTaVWC5 (EFA = 125 (eV/atom)−1), HfNbTaTiZrC5 (EFA = 100 (eV/atom)−1), and HfNbTaTiVC5 (EFA = 100 (eV/atom)−1) would form homogeneous single phases, while HfMoVWZrC5 (EFA = 37 (eV/atom)−1) would not.; Six of the nine synthesized compositions (MoNbTaVWC5, HfNbTaTiZrC5, HfNbTaTiVC5, HfNbTaTiWC5, NbTaTiVWC5, HfTaTiWZrC5) exhibited single rock-salt fcc phases, whereas the three lowest-EFA compositions showed multiple secondary phases.; Vickers hardness of HfNbTaTiZrC5 reached 32 GPa, which is 50% higher than the rule of mixtures (ROM) prediction, and HfTaTiWZrC5 reached 33 GPa.; The Pearson correlation between the inverse EFA (EFA−1) and lattice distortion (ε) was 0.97, and the Spearman rank correlation was 0.98, validating EFA as a synthesizability descriptor.; Lattice distortion (ε) ranged from 0.063% for MoNbTaVWC5 (most homogeneous) to 0.325% for HfMoVWZrC5 (least homogeneous).; The highest-EFA composition MoNbTaVWC5 formed a homogeneous phase despite using precursors Mo2C and W2C with different structures (orthorhombic and hexagonal) and stoichiometries compared to the rock-salt product.; Vibrational contributions to formation free energy at 2000 K ranged from ~0 meV/atom to −31 meV/atom, which are significantly smaller than the configurational entropy contributions required to overcome formation enthalpy barriers (50–150 meV/atom).; A threshold of EFA ~50 (eV/atom)−1 was identified as the point above which homogeneous disordered single phases are likely to form.. Mechanism: The authors argue that a narrow energy distribution spectrum (low standard deviation σ) implies a low energy cost to access metastable configurations, promoting configurational randomness (entropy) at finite temperatures. This entropy stabilization allows the disordered rock-salt phase to remain locked in upon cooling, even when competing ordered phases exist. Enhanced hardness is attributed to mass disorder causing impedance mismatch that scatters dislocations, increasing resistance to plastic deformation.. Limitations: The study notes that the Williamson–Hall formalism does not provide particularly accurate absolute values of lattice strain (ε), though it is effective for relative comparisons. Additionally, the vibrational contribution to entropy is an order of magnitude smaller than configurational entropy, and the study did not investigate the specific effect of carbon stoichiometry on melting points..
